logline: A disgraced Indian intelligence operative turned literature professor is pulled back into a covert mission to rescue captured agents from Taliban-held Balochistan.

bollymeter.basis: Rotten Tomatoes critics scored it at 36 percent from 11 reviews, citing weak scripting and uneven direction despite capable performers; the 86-percent audience Popcornmeter reflects a fan base more forgiving of the genre mechanics than professional critics were.

seasons.review_body: Bard of Blood launched September 27, 2019 as a Red Chillies Entertainment production adapted from Bilal Siddiqi's novel. Emraan Hashmi plays Kabir Anand, a RAW operative suspended after a Balochistan operation goes wrong, now a small-town Shakespeare teacher who is activated for an unsanctioned rescue mission. The spy-thriller framework is competent and the Balochistan location work atmospheric, but critics clustered on the same fault: a script that buries its capable cast under plot mechanics that are neither surprising enough to satisfy genre fans nor character-driven enough to build tension organically. Rotten Tomatoes registered 36 percent positive from 11 reviews - notably at odds with an 86-percent audience Popcornmeter. Scroll.in found it pauperised by a script devoid of humour; The News Minute cited weak writing and a director seeming to figure things out mid-production. Hashmi's commitment to the role drew consistent acknowledgement even in negative reviews.
